answer: The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 240 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. Because the timing is recorded against the atlas challenge, the tide audit can replay the inlet history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. A scripted farm hence has to pad 78 submissions and hold each account open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
